recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Highbridge shooting, deadly Manhattan discovery, missing senior
recentItems.description:
A 43-year-old man is in critical condition and two women are recovering after a shooting on University Avenue in Highbridge. Police are also investigating the death of 27-year-old Lovay Williams, who was found with wounds to her face and neck inside a Manhattan home. Jury selection is expected to begin for three men charged in the 2022 killings of Nikki Huang and Jessie Parilla. Other incidents include a shooting in Concourse Village, a stabbing at the Fordham Road station, the search for missing Bronx resident Daniel Driscoll, a cleanup of a long-troubled Throggs Neck property, and upcoming traffic changes tied to a new Tremont Avenue busway.

recentItems.title: Thieves crash into dealership, steal vehicle from showroom
recentItems.description:
Police are asking for the public’s help after suspects broke into Nissan 112 on Route 112 in Medford around 1:30 a.m. Investigators say the thieves stole keys to a 2023 BMW, used it to crash into a 2022 Nissan that struck the building and shattered a window, then took a 2023 Dodge from inside the showroom before fleeing. Employees say it is the third vehicle theft at the dealership this year, and police are also investigating similar incidents in the area.

recentItems.title: Bronx officer injured when firearm discharges while leaving home
recentItems.description:
An off-duty NYPD officer, identified by family as 33-year-old Demitrious Caceres, is recovering after police say he accidentally shot himself in the leg inside his Bronx home on Bailey Avenue in the Kingsbridge neighborhood. Family members say the firearm discharged as Caceres was attempting to conceal it in a holster before leaving. Investigators are examining how the weapon was being handled when it went off, and the investigation remains ongoing.

recentItems.title: Queens woman arrested in nearly $1 million senior scam
recentItems.description:
A 70-year-old Hicksville, New York woman wired nearly $1 million after allegedly being told she was involved in a crime in India and needed to send money to resolve it. Investigators say the suspect claimed to be with the Delhi Police Department and later demanded an additional $300,000 in gold bars. Nassau County police arrested a Queens woman during a sting operation after the victim reported the alleged scam.

recentItems.title: Over 600 FDNY members lost to 9/11-related illnesses, report shows
recentItems.description:
Twenty-five years after the Sept. 11 attacks, the FDNY says the health impact on first responders continues. A new report details medical monitoring of firefighters and EMS personnel who responded to Lower Manhattan, where more than 600 members have died from 9/11-related illnesses. Officials say ongoing treatment and monitoring have improved survival rates, quality of life and outcomes for those dealing with cancer, PTSD, depression, and respiratory symptoms.

recentItems.title: The Man in the Red Bandana: Students Inspired by 9/11 hero's lasting legacy
recentItems.description:
Welles Crowther, known as "The Man in the Red Bandana," died helping others escape one of the Twin Towers on September 11 before the building collapsed. His story, featured in the documentary The Man in the Red Bandana, continues to inspire acts of kindness and leadership. Students at Pleasantville Middle School received green bandanas as a reminder that even small actions can make a difference.

Original airdate: Sept. 19, 2017

recentItems.title: NYC’s mysterious Hart Island reveals its stories
recentItems.description:
Just a half-mile ferry ride from City Island, Hart Island feels worlds away from New York City. Public tours now give visitors a chance to learn about the island's history, including public burials, incarcerated workers who helped bury the dead, and the lingering mystery surrounding 33 people who died from AIDS-related complications. Rangers say the island's story is ultimately a New York story, connecting the city's past and present.

recentItems.title: Childhood friend steps up to save former News 12 reporter’s life with liver donation
recentItems.description:
After battling autoimmune hepatitis and primary biliary cholangitis for most of her life, former News 12 reporter Amy McGorry desperately needed a new liver. When childhood friend Susan Filshie saw Amy's story, she stepped forward, underwent testing, and was found to be a perfect donor match. Three months after their transplant surgery, both women are recovering and hope their journey inspires others to learn about living organ donation.
